name: Prawn Masala
cuisine: Maharashtrian coastal (Mumbai Koli / Malvani–Konkan style, semi-dry)

ingredients.name: Prawns (jhinga / kolambi), medium, peeled and deveined, raw
Salt (namak)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ tsp in total (1 g / a scant ¼ tsp in the marinade, 1.5 g / ¼ tsp in the masala)

ingredients.name: Water (for kokum and masala)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 tbsp warm water for the kokum + 1 tbsp for the spices + 2 tbsp at the end

ingredients.name: Onion (pyaaz), finely chopped
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 small-medium onion, about ½ cup chopped

ingredients.name: Tomato (tamatar), finely chopped
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 small tomato, about ⅓ cup chopped

equipment: Small kadai or heavy pan (about 20 cm) with a lid
Small sharp knife or kitchen scissors, for deveining
Two bowls (one for the cleaned prawns and marinade, one for shells and veins) and a colander
Small bowl or cup, for soaking the kokum
Kitchen scale (useful for weighing 150 g cleaned prawns)
Optional: mortar and pestle, or a small grinder jar, to crush fresh ginger and garlic

steps.title: Thaw (frozen prawns only)
steps.text: Put the frozen prawns in a sealed zip bag and sink the bag in a bowl of cold water.
steps.tip: Never thaw prawns in hot water or leave them out on the counter; the outside starts to cook or spoil before the inside thaws. Already peeled and deveined? Skip to step 5.
steps.visualCue: The prawns are soft and bendy, with no ice in the middle
steps.cameraCheck: The bag in the bowl of water
steps.videoShot: A zip bag of frozen prawns being pushed under cold water.

steps.title: Remove the heads (whole prawns only)
steps.text: Hold the body, and twist and pull off each head.
steps.visualCue: A pile of heads in the waste bowl; headless bodies in the other
steps.cameraCheck: The headless prawns
steps.videoShot: Fingers twisting a head off a grey prawn.

steps.title: Peel off the shell and legs
steps.text: Pull off the legs from the underside, then peel the shell off in rings. Pull or pinch off the tail, or leave it on for looks.
steps.tip: Keep the shells and heads in the freezer if you like stock; they are not used here.
steps.visualCue: Smooth, grey-translucent prawn meat with no shell bits
steps.cameraCheck: One peeled prawn on your palm
steps.videoShot: A thumb sliding the shell rings off a prawn.

steps.title: Devein
steps.text: Make a shallow slit (2–3 mm deep) along the curved back of each prawn with a knife tip or scissors, and lift out the thin dark thread (the vein, which is the gut) with the knife tip or a toothpick. Check the underside too; some prawns have a thin second vein there.
steps.tip: The vein is not harmful, but it can be gritty and bitter; always remove it on medium and large prawns.
steps.visualCue: No dark line visible along the back
steps.cameraCheck: A deveined prawn with the slit open
steps.videoShot: A toothpick lifting a dark vein out of the slit.

steps.title: Rinse and drain
steps.text: Rinse the cleaned prawns twice in cold water, drain in the colander, and pat dry with a paper towel or clean cloth. Weigh out 150 g.
steps.tip: Wash your hands, knife and board with soap after handling raw seafood.
steps.visualCue: Clean prawns that look matte, not dripping
steps.cameraCheck: 150 g prawns on the scale
steps.videoShot: Prawns tumbling into a colander under running water.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: In a bowl, mix the prawns with ¼ tsp (0.5 g) turmeric, ½ tsp (1 g) Kashmiri chilli powder and a scant ¼ tsp (1 g) salt. Cover and refrigerate.
steps.tip: Don't marinate prawns with salt for hours; 10–30 min is enough, and longer can make them watery.
steps.visualCue: Every prawn coated evenly orange-red
steps.cameraCheck: The marinated prawns in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Fingers tossing the prawns in the red-yellow spice.

steps.title: Soak the kokum
steps.text: Put 2–3 kokum petals (3 g) in a cup with 2 tbsp (30 ml) warm water.
steps.visualCue: The water turns deep pink-purple
steps.cameraCheck: The kokum in its cup
steps.videoShot: Dark kokum petals sinking into water that slowly turns pink.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Finely chop 80 g onion.
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces (about rice-grain to lentil size)
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped onion on the board
steps.videoShot: A knife rocking through onion slices.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Finely chop 60 g tomato.
steps.visualCue: Small juicy cubes
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped tomato
steps.videoShot: A knife dicing a tomato.

steps.title: Prepare the aromatics
steps.text: Slit 1 green chilli lengthwise. Get 1½ tsp (8 g) ginger-garlic paste ready. Measure 1 heaped tsp (4 g) Malvani masala and ½ tsp (1 g) coriander powder into a small bowl.
steps.tip: Malvani masala burns quickly; having it measured before you start keeps step 15 calm.
steps.visualCue: Everything laid out near the stove
steps.cameraCheck: The paste, chilli and spice bowl
steps.videoShot: A spoon levelling the Malvani masala.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Heat 2 tsp (10 ml) oil in the kadai on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers and flows easily
steps.cameraCheck: The kadai with oil
steps.videoShot: Oil swirling in the pan.

steps.title: Add curry leaves
steps.text: Add 6–8 curry leaves.
steps.tip: Pat the leaves dry first and stand back; wet leaves spit.
steps.visualCue: They crackle and turn bright green, then slightly crisp
steps.cameraCheck: The leaves in the oil
steps.videoShot: Curry leaves spluttering as they hit the oil.

steps.title: Fry the onion
steps.text: Add the 80 g chopped onion and sauté, stirring often.
steps.visualCue: Soft and light golden-brown at the edges, with a sweet smell
steps.cameraCheck: The golden onions
steps.videoShot: The spatula turning golden onions.

steps.title: Add ginger-garlic and green chilli
steps.text: Add the 8 g ginger-garlic paste and the slit chilli. Stir.
steps.visualCue: The raw garlic smell is gone; the paste looks lightly golden
steps.cameraCheck: The onion with the paste mixed in
steps.videoShot: The paste melting into the onion.

steps.title: Add the spice powders
steps.text: Lower the heat to low, add the Malvani masala and coriander powder with 1 tbsp (15 ml) water, and stir.
steps.tip: The splash of water stops the masala burning. If it smells sharp or bitter, the heat is too high.
steps.visualCue: A dark red paste with oil starting to show at the edges; a toasty smell, no burnt smell
steps.cameraCheck: The red masala in the pan
steps.videoShot: Spice powders hitting the onion, followed by a splash of water.

steps.title: Cook the tomato
steps.text: Add the 60 g chopped tomato and 1.5 g (¼ tsp) salt. Raise to medium and cook, mashing with the spatula.
steps.visualCue: The tomato melts into a thick, glossy paste and oil separates at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The finished masala base
steps.videoShot: The spatula pressing tomato into the masala.

steps.title: Add the prawns
steps.text: Add the marinated prawns with any spice left in the bowl. Toss to coat.
steps.visualCue: All prawns coated in masala; they start turning pink at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The prawns in the masala
steps.videoShot: Prawns tipped into the red masala and tossed.

steps.title: Add kokum and simmer covered
steps.text: Pour in the kokum with its soaking water, plus 2 tbsp (30 ml) water. Stir, cover and cook on low-medium heat.
steps.tip: A tight "O" curl means they are overcooked and will be rubbery; take them off sooner next time. Large prawns may need 1–2 min more.
steps.visualCue: The prawns are pink and opaque all the way through and have curled into a loose "C"
steps.cameraCheck: One prawn cut in half (opaque white inside, no grey glassy centre)
steps.videoShot: The lid lifting to show pink, curled prawns in bubbling masala.

steps.title: Reduce to semi-dry
steps.text: Uncover and cook on medium heat, stirring gently.
steps.tip: Want it drier (sukka)? Reduce 1 min more. Want a thin rassa for rice? Add 3–4 tbsp hot water and simmer 1 min. Lift out the kokum petals now if you don't want to bite into one.
steps.visualCue: The masala clings to the prawns, with only 1–2 tbsp of thick gravy left in the pan
steps.cameraCheck: The pan tilted to show the thick masala
steps.videoShot: The spatula drawing a line through the masala that holds for a second.

steps.title: Finish and rest
steps.text: Turn off the heat, scatter 1 tbsp chopped coriander leaves, cover and leave to rest.
steps.visualCue: Glossy, deep red prawns flecked with green
steps.cameraCheck: The finished bowl
steps.videoShot: Coriander falling onto the red prawn masala.

reasons: about 33 g of lean protein for about 290 kcal, with very little saturated fat, no frying and only 2 tsp of oil. Onion, tomato, curry leaves and spices add fibre and vitamins C, A and K, and prawns are rich in selenium, B12, phosphorus and some omega-3. Points come off for cholesterol (about 240 mg, about 80% of the usual 300 mg guidance), sodium (about 1,160 mg) and little vegetable volume. Restaurant versions usually use much more oil (often coconut oil, which is high in saturated fat), more salt, sometimes red colour, and are eaten with large portions of white rice or pav.

researchRating.basis: prawn masala is a fixture of Mumbai's Malvani, Koli and Gomantak lunch homes. It is repeatedly named a must-order at Chaitanya (Dadar), Gajalee, Pal's Fish and Highway Gomantak in Mumbai food guides (Homegrown, Curly Tales, CNN Travel, LBB, Slurrp, independent food blogs), and every major Indian recipe site and chef publishes a version (Flavors of Mumbai, Yummy Tummy Aarthi, Kali Mirch by Smita, Sanjeev Kapoor, The Quint's Malvani recipe). Small deduction: published recipe star ratings and review counts could not be collected in this run (sites blocked direct access), and reviews often complain of rubbery, overcooked prawns at home and inconsistent prawn size and price in restaurants.

storage: Cool within 1 hour and refrigerate in a closed box; eat within 1–2 days (seafood keeps for less time than meat). Freezer: up to 1 month, but prawns turn firmer and slightly rubbery after freezing and reheating. Reheat only once, in a covered pan on low heat with 1–2 tbsp water for 2–3 min until just hot. Don't boil it, or the prawns toughen. Microwave on medium in 30-second bursts. Raw cleaned prawns keep 1 day in the fridge; freeze them if you are not cooking that day.
leftoverRemix: prawn masala pav-wrap (kolambi frankie). Roughly chop the leftover prawns in their masala, warm in a pan until dry, and roll into a hot chapati with sliced onion, a little green chutney, chaat masala and lemon. Or toss with leftover rice, a few curry leaves and a fried egg for a quick prawn masala fried rice. Use within the same 1–2 day window and reheat only once.
burnOff: about 4.1 km of running (290 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 5.8 km of brisk walking (about 1 hour 10 minutes at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With 150 g rice (about 485 kcal), about 6.9 km of running.

navratri.reason: contains prawns, onion, garlic and table salt, all avoided in the common Navratri vrat rule set.

ekadashi.reason: contains prawns and onion-garlic, avoided under the common Ekadashi rule set (same as Navratri in the sources used).

jain.reason: contains prawns, plus onion, garlic and ginger (root).

ramadan.reason: seafood needs no halal slaughter, so there is no meat-sourcing swap. Islamic schools differ on whether prawns are permitted, so follow your own practice. High-protein and light for iftar, but at about 1,160 mg sodium (est.) it is salty for sehri unless you halve the salt.

jain.reason: contains prawns, plus onion, garlic and ginger.

pescatarian.reason: the only animal food is prawns (seafood); no meat, egg or dairy.

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, rava, maida or besan, and no hing (asafoetida). Packaged Malvani/Koli masala blends vary, so check the label for wheat or hing (most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour).

dairyFree.reason: no curd, cream, butter or ghee; cooked in oil.

description: A non-veg, pescatarian, gluten-free and dairy-free Mumbai semi-dry prawn masala, soured with kokum; vegetarian (mushroom) and low-oil versions below.

variants.reason: the Jain diet excludes all seafood, so there is no Jain prawn masala. The dish also relies on onion, garlic and ginger.
the dish is defined by prawns. The plant-based route is the Vegetarian (mushroom) variant below, which is already vegan because the recipe has no dairy.
main recipe already gluten-free (no flour or hing). Check the label of the Malvani/Koli masala, since some blends may contain hing or flour.
main recipe already dairy-free (cooked in oil, no curd, cream or ghee).
